content: Recent publications have explored the application of Geometric Algebra (GA) to the modeling, analysis, and control of dynamical systems, with a particular focus on electrical circuits. A central component of this approach involves transforming the ordinary differential equations governing system behavior from the real domain into the Laplace domain. Achieving this transformation necessitates a well-defined Laplace transform within the context of GA. In this work, we extend previous research that generalized the Laplace transform to certain hyper-complex algebras by providing a definition of the Laplace transform specifically tailored to Geometric Algebra. Our formulation and its associated properties are valid for geometric algebras with signature up to and including 5.

"""
Recent publications have begun to investigate the use of Geometric Algebra (GA) in the modeling, analysis, and control of dynamical systems, particularly electrical circuits. A key aspect of this process is transforming the ordinary differential equations that describe system behavior from the real domain to the Laplace domain. This transformation requires a definition of the Laplace transform within GA. In this work, we build upon previous studies that extended the Laplace transform to certain hyper-complex algebras by introducing a definition of the Laplace transform specifically within the framework of Geometric Algebra. Our definition and its associated properties are applicable to geometric algebras with signature less than or equal to 5.
